newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU envoy won't push for seat at Middle East talks.
newsitem.headline: EU envoy won't push for seat at Middle East talks.

text.p: The European Union's new Middle East envoy said on Tuesday he aimed to act as a political go-between, provide economic aid and calm a heated atmosphere rather than push a French bid for an EU seat at peace talks.

"I believe one sits around the negotiating table only when one is invited to do so by all the parties," Miguel Angel Moratinos, Spain's ambassador to Israel, told a Radio France International interviewer.

"I believe that the role of the Union is not so much to sit at a table as to transmit political messages and show one's economic and financial availability," added Moratinos, who was appointed to the EU envoy post on Monday by the bloc's foreign ministers.
He had just been questioned on whether he would relay France's position -- that Europe should sit alongside the United States in peace talks -- when he began his mission.

Israel, convinced that French President Jacques Chirac is too pro-Arab after he toured the region last week, has ruled out a European presence at its peace talks with the Palestine Liberation Organisation.
"I will relay the position of the 15 (EU members). There is a French position, there is a British position," Moratinos said.

"I believe that in a region where passions rule...one must try to lower the (political) temperature...create a climate of confidence and mutual trust which will help inhabitants and leaders take difficult decisions which are risky but absolutely necessary for their peoples," he said.
The French foreign ministry welcomed Moratinos' appointment but did not reiterate Chirac's call for an EU seat at the peace talks. It also praised U.S. President Bill Clinton's envoy.
The appointment "will help increase the coherence and efficiency of Europe's action," the French ministry's spokesman, Jacques Rummelhardt, told a news briefing.

He also said it would "usefully reinforce the action of the peace partners, including that of the American coordinator Dennis Ross." Rummelhardt praised Ross' "courageous efforts" to bring the Israelis and Palestinians together.
